analysis.title: Weekly HF Highlights: HFs Reluctant to Add Risk Amidst Macro Overhang, Bid for AI Slows
key_insights: Hedge funds were reluctant to add risk this week amid macro and geopolitical overhang, giving a quieter week for volumes and themes. HFs ended as small net sellers of global equities, with selling spread across N. America, Europe and APAC.
US L/S net leverage was flat WoW at 52%, which is 56th %-tile since 2010. Gross leverage ticked up to 207%, 91st %-tile since 2010 but near 12-month troughs (2nd %-tile on a 1-year basis).
US Energy has been net sold in 13 of the past 15 sessions after consistent buying in July and August. Crude-levered equities drive much of the supply, and HFs are also net sellers of E&Ps.
Positioning differs within Energy: net exposure to crude-levered equities is still quite elevated, while E&P net exposure is at roughly 12-month lows.
HFs were net sellers of Health Care, led by MedTech and Life Science Tools. They continued to trim gross across both crowded Biotech longs (MSXXBIOC) and crowded Biotech shorts (MSXXBIOS).

TMT flows were mixed. HFs bought Infrastructure Software (MSXXINSW) and Cybersecurity (MSXXCYBR), while Agentic AI (MSXXCLAW) and AI Tech Beneficiaries (MSXXAIB) ended net sold, though in smaller amounts.

Factor flow was muted, with a small bias toward buying Quality and Size, consistent with the trailing ~2 months. Positioning in SMID-caps remains near recent lows because short exposure is elevated across all HF strategies, on the back of pressure in the rates space.
HFs were net sellers of EU equities through short additions. Both US-based and EU-based HFs added shorts rather than unwinding longs. HF net exposure to EU equities is near record lows.

EU-based HFs are running the most overweight US equities relative to EU equities in 5 years of history. They have begun selling US longs and have moved some of that capital into European short ideas, but have not yet become buyers of EU equities.

APAC equities were sold in lighter amounts, led by supply in China and India. HFs were smaller buyers of Korea and Taiwan but did not re-engage in Global Memory (MSXXGMEM) names and continue to net sell the theme.
In Japan, HFs reduced directional risk in Consumer and were smaller buyers of TMT.
September was a challenging month: the average global HF fund was down about 60bps, leaving funds up about 7% for the year. Equity L/S funds in the US, Europe and Asia were each down roughly 1.5%.
Americas L/S funds were -1.6% in September and +8.4% YTD through Q3, versus S&P 500 +12.7% YTD. Dispersion is wide, with the 75th %-tile fund at about +16% and the 25th %-tile fund at about -2.2%.
European funds average +5.4% YTD and EU-based L/S funds are +3.5%, versus Euro STOXX 600 +10.2%. Asia-based funds (all strategies) and Asia-based L/S funds are both up about 8% YTD.
Top 50 crowding longs minus shorts returned +0.6% WTD, +0.1% MTD and +24.4% YTD in N. America. In Europe the spread is -0.22% WTD (Longs -3.04%, Shorts -2.82%), and in Asia it is -0.64% WTD.

sector_views.rationale: HFs net sold US Energy in 13 of the past 15 sessions, led by crude-levered equities, though their net exposure remains elevated versus E&Ps near 12-month lows.
HFs were net sellers, driven by MedTech and Life Science Tools, and trimmed gross on both crowded Biotech longs and shorts.
Flows were mixed. HFs bought Infrastructure Software and Cybersecurity and were smaller net sellers of Agentic AI and AI Tech Beneficiaries.

risk_factors: Macro and geopolitical overhang is keeping HFs from adding risk.
Pressure in the rates space has raised short exposure to SMID-caps across HF strategies.
Oil price moves are driving continued de-risking of US Energy.
Wide performance dispersion among Americas L/S funds, with the 25th %-tile fund down about 2.2% YTD.
charts_described: Key stats list US L/S net leverage at 52% (56th %-tile since 2010) and gross at 207% (91st %-tile since 2010).
Regional leverage table: Europe gross 172% and net 53%, Asia gross 127% and net 63%.
vol_and_positioning: US L/S net leverage is 52% (-1% WoW, 56th %-tile since 2010) and gross leverage is 207% (+1% WoW, 91st %-tile since 2010).
Europe gross leverage is 172% (25th %-tile since 2010) and net leverage is 53% (91st %-tile since 2010, -2% WoW). Asia gross is 127% and net is 63% (68th %-tile since 2010).
HF net exposure to EU equities is near record lows, and EU-based HFs are the most overweight US equities versus EU equities in the last 5 years.
SMID-cap positioning is near recent lows because of elevated short exposure across all HF strategies amid pressure in the rates space.
Crowded Biotech longs (MSXXBIOC) and shorts (MSXXBIOS) both saw gross trimmed. Top 50 crowded longs have returned +38.44% YTD versus +13.99% for top 50 shorts in N. America.
geopolitical: The report cites a macro and geopolitical overhang as the reason HFs were reluctant to add risk this week, without naming specific events.
Oil prices remain very much in focus for HF energy positioning.
